transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because I keep hearing these voices. It's... it's as clear as somebody standing right next to me in my little studio. They keep saying my name, and telling me that my work is being judged. And this is happening even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody else is there. I just needed to see someone about it.
When did you first start hearing these voices? Was it sudden, or did it develop gradually over time?

It started about nine months ago. The voices, and... well, this constant fear I have that my work is being watched... they've both been happening for about nine months now. I'd say it didn't just happen all at once overnight, it sort of built up a bit, but it's been a solid nine months of dealing with it.

Before these voices and the feeling of being watched started nine months ago, would you say you were functioning well overall—like doing your work, managing daily life, and relationships without major problems?

Before all this started? Yeah, I'd say I was doing fine before then. I was managing. But once the voices and the fear set in... well, things really went downhill. 

I got to the point where my job as a personal care aide was in real danger. I started missing my shifts, and... I'd mix up my care notes. I just couldn't keep my client visits organized the way I used to. And my life outside of work just stopped. I quit going to my walking club, and I used to go to these art talks at the library, but I stopped going to those too. So I've just been mostly alone at home.

When you're talking with people or trying to communicate, have others mentioned that what you're saying doesn't make sense or is hard to follow? Or have you noticed your own thoughts feeling jumbled or disorganized?

No, I don't think so. People seem to understand me just fine when I do talk to them. I mean... nobody has ever told me that I don't make sense or that I'm hard to follow. 

My thoughts aren't really jumbled up, either. I know exactly what I want to say. It's just... well, it can be a little hard to concentrate sometimes with the voices going on, but my own thoughts are clear.

You mentioned feeling like your work is being watched and judged. Do you have specific beliefs about who might be watching you or why they're doing this? Are there particular people or organizations you think are behind it?

Well, yeah, I do have an idea about who's doing it. I... I got it in my head that it's this other home-care agency in town, and also some of the people from the library. 

I know they've been watching my paintings and looking at my client papers. They're trying to steal an opportunity, like a chance that was meant for me. I know it sounds strange to other people. Folks have told me it doesn't make any sense, but... I just know they're doing it. I can't shake it.

When you think back to nine months ago when this all started, did the voices come first, or did you already have the feeling that people were watching and judging your work before you started hearing the voices?

They actually started right around the same time. It's been about nine months now that I've been dealing with both the voices and that strong feeling—the fear, really—that my work is being watched and judged by those people. It all just kind of hit me together nine months ago.
Over these past nine months, have you noticed any changes in how you dress, bathe, or take care of yourself? Or have people commented on your behavior being odd or unusual in some way?

Well, I still get dressed and take care of myself fine. But... as far as my behavior, I guess I have been doing some odd things, especially at work. 

There have been times during my client visits where I'll just completely stop what I'm supposed to be doing. I'll take things like the medical gloves, or those little plastic pill cups, and some of my crochet scraps, and I'll just start lining them all up in patterns on the table. Or... sometimes I'll just stand out in the hallway, staring, almost like I'm waiting for some kind of signal. I just stop working and do that instead. So, yeah, I suppose that is pretty unusual.

When you're lining up those objects in patterns or standing in the hallway waiting for a signal, do you feel like you're doing this because the people watching you want you to do it, or does it just feel like something you need to do without a clear reason why?

I guess it's a bit of both, honestly. I don't always have a clear reason why I do it, but... I just feel this strong pull to do it. Like I mentioned, I'll be right in the middle of a client visit, and I'll just stop. I'll take the medical gloves, the little pill cups, maybe some crochet scraps I have with me, and I just have to arrange them in these patterns. Or I'll end up out in the hallway, just standing there, staring... waiting for a signal, I guess. It just feels like something I have to do in that moment.

Over these nine months, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, excited, or like your mood was really high or expansive? And during those times, did you notice you needed less sleep than usual, or that you were doing a lot more activities or projects than you normally would?

Yeah, I have had times like that. I'll go from feeling so... well, just so bright and chosen, like I have all these big plans and the whole town of Greenville just can't hold them all. I get real energetic. 

But then... it can change fast. I'll go from feeling that high to snapping hard at someone over a real small thing. Like, if one of my clients just asks me to repeat myself, I'll just snap right at them. So, yes, my mood does get really high like you said, but it gets real irritable, too.
When you have those periods where you feel really energetic and high, with big plans and everything, how long do those periods usually last? Are we talking hours, days, a week or more?

Well, those stretches where I'm all charged up... where I'm sleeping very little and just chasing after all these big plans... they usually last a while. I'd say they've been coming and going like that for about 11 months now. They definitely last for days or weeks at a time, not just a few hours.

When you're not in one of those high-energy periods—when your mood is more normal and stable—do you still hear those voices and feel like people are watching you? Or do the voices and that feeling of being watched mainly happen during those times when you're feeling really energetic and have all those big plans?

They still happen even when my mood is normal. I remember... well, there was a time after my energy finally dropped and I was sleeping more normally again. I thought maybe things would quiet down. But the voices kept right on going. And that feeling I had that people were judging me, or tracking what I was doing at work... it just kept happening for several weeks, even though I felt completely normal and calm otherwise. So, yeah, it's not just when I have all that energy.
